title: chore: enable agent publishing for MCP quest contributors
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds afanasevmylife (#15032) and Marcus-Mok-GH (#15262) to the existing community model/agent publishing allowlist.
- Recognizes the selected MCP installer and a similar focused alternative; existing publishers are unchanged.
- Verified GitHub IDs, allowlist uniqueness, and formatting. Two-line data change only.

Addresses #15014

gist.headline: Two new garden keys
gist.blurb: Two MCP Quest contributors now have the keys to publish their agents. The garden gets a couple more careful hands, which is how ecosystems avoid becoming parking lots.
gist.summary: Added the verified GitHub IDs afanasevmylife and Marcus-Mok-GH to the community model and agent publishing allowlist for selected MCP Quest contributor agents.
gist.impact: The selected MCP installer and a focused alternative can now publish through the existing contributor flow, while the established publisher allowlist remains unchanged.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy community publishing scene: Polli welcomes two small contributor seed packets into a guarded garden gate marked for MCP agents, with a retro terminal showing a neat approved-ID list. The gate and growing code-plants represent the verified allowlist; Polli wears a tiny librarian keyring to show careful access rather than a broad new permission system.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute pixel bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings, wearing a tiny librarian keyring as she unlocks a small garden gate for two labeled contributor seed packets beside sprouting code-plants and a retro terminal with simple pixel text “MCP OK”; use lime green (#ecf874) prominently with warm cream, mint, lavender, and peach pastels. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, chunky sprites, subtle CRT glow, nostalgic but emotionally warm.
